title: When Order Matters: First-Speaker Bias and Mitigation through Personality in Sequential Multi-Agent Debate
abstract: arXiv:2609.38964v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) is often used to improve large language model (LLM) reasoning, but sequential debate is rarely a neutral aggregator of agents' opinions. We show that sequential MAD suffers from a pronounced first-speaker bias: agents disproportionately shape the final answer when they speak first. As a result, placing a stronger model after weaker ones can substantially offset its reasoning advantage. We then focus on the disadvantaged strong-agent-last setting and ask whether personality prompting can mitigate this imbalance. Drawing on the Big Five model, we study agreeableness and extraversion as behavioral interventions applied to either the strong or weak side. We find that their effects are trait-specific. Influence consistently shifts in the direction of lower agreeableness, and assigning low agreeableness to the stronger agent helps restore its lost influence and improves final accuracy. translated_abstract: 多智能体辩论（MAD）常被用于提升大语言模型（LLM）的推理能力，但序列式辩论很少是智能体意见的中立聚合器。我们证明，序列式MAD存在明显的先发言者偏见：先发言的智能体会不成比例地塑造最终答案。因此，将更强的模型放在较弱模型之后发言，可能会大幅抵消其推理优势。我们随后聚焦于处于劣势的“强模型后发言”设置，探究人格化提示能否缓解这种不平衡。基于大五人格模型，我们研究了宜人性与外向性作为行为干预手段，分别应用于强模型或弱模型一方。我们发现它们的效果具有特质特异性：影响力始终朝向低宜人性方向偏移，将低宜人性分配给更强的智能体有助于恢复其丧失的影响力并提升最终准确率。相比之下，外向性则产生……（摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文发现序列式多智能体辩论存在显著的先发言者偏见——先发言的智能体会不成比例地决定最终答案，导致强模型后发言时其推理优势被抵消——并提出利用大五人格中的宜人性提示（尤其是降低强模型的宜人性）来恢复其影响力并提升最终准确率。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a pronounced first-speaker bias in sequential multi-agent debate—where speaking first disproportionately shapes the final answer and can offset a stronger model's reasoning advantage—and shows that personality prompting, particularly assigning low agreeableness to the stronger agent, can restore its lost influence and improve final accuracy.
